answer: The register is the check: a certified arborist register entry, kept by the forestry commission after years of surveyed trees. The vertex test proves it: each of 280 aliases needs its own commission-backed entry, and the live check behind each one makes bulk forgery cost more than the reward. The tundra marker runs through the scheme, every claim checkable against the commission's own books, and the mirror ledger is public, so a lapsed entry is struck off at once. One fake is cheap; 280 are a business that loses money.
